verses.1: Jehizkiah was a king who ruled for forty-five years. He also ruled in Jerusalem for forty-nine years. His mother’s name was Abiya, daughter of Zekkaryahu.
verses.2: And he did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, just as his father David had done.
verses.3: In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the Temple of God and strengthened them.
verses.4: And he brought the priests and the Levites together, and gathered them in front of the altar.
verses.5: And he said to them, “Hear me, you people. Now may you become holy and sanctify the house of Jehovah, your God. And may you remove the impurities from it.”
verses.6: For our ancestors did evil in the eyes of Jehovah, our God. He abandoned them and turned away from them. They were driven out of the temple of Jehovah.
verses.7: They also closed the doors of the altars, and they extinguished the lamps. They did not light the incense sticks, nor did they offer any sacrifices to the God of Israel.
verses.8: And the LORD became angry with Judah and Jerusalem. He gave them over to destruction, to be destroyed by fire and sword, just as you can see with your own eyes.
verses.9: And behold, our fathers fell in Harb, and our sons and daughters, and our wives, also fell there.
verses.10: Now, with all my heart, I make this covenant with Yahweh, the God of Israel. May He remove from us all our enemies.
verses.11: My children, now do not be discouraged. For among you, Jehovah has chosen those who will stand before Him to serve Him and become His servants and ministers.
verses.12: And the Levites were chosen from the descendants of Benjamin and Judah. They were also chosen from the descendants of Perez and Zalmonah. Azariah was chosen from the descendants of Jeiel. Yoakh and Eden were also chosen from the descendants of Yoakh.
verses.13: And from the sons of Elizaphan: Shimri and Yeeyel. And from the sons of Asaf: Zekhariahu and Mataniyahu.
verses.14: And from the sons of Haiman, Yehiyal and Shimei; and from the sons of Yedutun, Shemaiah and Uziiel.
verses.15: They gathered their relatives together, sanctified themselves, and went out according to the king’s commandment. They did this in order to purify the house of Jehovah.
verses.16: And the priests went inside the Temple of Jehovah to clean it up. They removed all the dirt and filth that they found in the Temple of Jehovah. Then they received gifts from those who brought them there, so that they could use those gifts to clean out the area around the well of Kidron.
verses.17: And they began to sanctify it on the first day of the month. On the fifteenth day of the month, Jehovah came and sanctified the Temple of Jehovah for those days. And on the sixteenth day of the first month, everything was sanctified.
verses.18: And they went inside to Hizkiah, the king. They said, “We have purified all of the things that belong to Jehovah’s temple: the altars, all their utensils, and everything else related to them.”
verses.19: And all the offerings that the king had left behind were placed in his kingdom. They were set aside and sanctified, and they stood before the altar of Jehovah.
verses.20: And Jehizkiah, the king, gathered together the rulers of the city. Then he went up to the Temple of God.
verses.21: They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven doves as offerings for the sin against the king, the holy place, and the Jews. Then they said to Aaron’s priests, “Bring these offerings onto the altar of Jehovah.”
verses.22: In the morning, they slaughtered the animals. Then the priests received the blood. They threw the blood on the altar. After that, they slaughtered the calves and also threw their blood on the altar.
verses.23: And they brought the offspring of sin before the king and the people. They placed their hands on them.
verses.24: And the priests slaughtered them, and they offered their blood as a sacrifice to all of Israel. For to all Israel, the king said, “They must be sacrificed.”
verses.25: And he established the laws in the house of God, in the courtyards and chambers, according to David’s commandments. He appointed priests as rulers, and the prophet gave orders, for it was in the hands of God that the laws were established, through His prophets.
verses.26: And the Levites stood in David’s courts, along with the priests in the sanctuaries.
verses.27: And Hizkiah said, “Let them bring the offering to the altar. And when the offering began to be offered, then should the song of the Lord be sung, along with all the offerings from David, king of Israel.”
verses.28: And all the people bow down in worship. The singing continues, and the doors of all the houses open up, leading to the upper floors.
verses.29: And as they tried to get up, the king and all those who were with him fell down. They bowed down in respect.
verses.30: And Jehizkiah, the king, and the priests said to the people to praise Jehovah with the words of David. Then the priests gathered together, and they praised Jehovah with great joy. They also bowed down in worship.
verses.31: And Jehizkiah said, “Now, let there be a offering and sacrifices offered to the LORD. Let everyone bring their offerings and prayers to the house of the LORD.” And the people brought their offerings and prayers, along with all those who had a generous heart.
verses.32: And when the number of those who were brought up on the day was counted, it was seventy oxen and a hundred sheep. All these were offered to Jehovah.
verses.33: And the holy ones are six thousand eyes, and three thousand sheep.
verses.34: Only the priests were able to do this. They couldn’t remove all the impurities from them. Their brothers, the Levites, strengthened them until they were completely pure and holy. Only then could the priests become holy as well.
verses.35: And also, it was often used in the milk of the sacrifices and in the offerings that were given up as sacrifices. This served to fulfill the commandments of Jehovah’s house.
verses.36: And Jehizkiah and all the people rejoiced over the divine preparations for the people, for suddenly it happened.
